owners.design-assets: Editable source artwork and retained design inputs
owners.docs-readme: Localized README and product documentation media
owners.test-suite: Automated test fixtures and regression coverage

classes.runtime-required: Runtime files directly or dynamically consumed by the product
classes.target-specific-runtime: Runtime payload that belongs to exactly one OS/architecture target
classes.source-of-truth: Editable or retained source used to produce runtime assets
classes.docs-marketing: Documentation, README, screenshot, or demonstration media
classes.compatibility-bridge: Versioned migration, rollback, or legacy-format support
classes.generated-cache: Deterministically generated or cached content that must remain ignored
classes.safety-tombstone: Minimal fail-fast replacement for a retired unsafe entry point
classes.legal: License or distribution notice with permanent retention requirements

pathRules.retentionReason: Built-in themes are runtime product capabilities.
README and state-guide previews; repository references and external raw links must be audited before retirement.
Retained Cloudling pointer-bridge source files; runtime logic is inlined into theme SVGs.
Editable or retained source artwork; never a packaging input.
Deterministic regression fixtures; test count or age is not retirement evidence.

entries.retentionReason: Asset license must be retained regardless of code references.
Hero animation linked by localized READMEs.
Canonical application icon used by packaging, Windows/Linux trays, localized READMEs, and runtime integrations.
Canonical Windows build and shell icon; packaged once as a physical extraResource and embedded into Windows executables by electron-builder.
Canonical 256px runtime icon used by Settings and served at the stable PWA icon URL.
Canonical 512px runtime icon used by Linux packaging and served at the stable PWA icon URL.

duplicatePayloadExemptions.reason: The states currently require different file-keyed offsets; consolidation is blocked pending a renderer and hit-geometry design.
